fixes.explanation: A feast is a fair guess, since it's a big occasion. But the LORD doesn't tie the light to one. He asks for oil "…to keep the lamps burning continually." (Leviticus 24:2). No party required. Those lamps are on the whole time.

Evening it is. Aaron tends the lamps "…from evening until morning." (Leviticus 24:3). That's the night shift, baker, and I have respect for anybody who works it. I'd need a very big timer and a lot of coffee.

Midnight is a real hour, but it's not the one the text gives. Aaron tends the lamps "…from evening until morning." (Leviticus 24:3). Evening is where it starts. Midnight is somewhere in the middle of that stretch, baker.
Noon is a fine time for a lot of jobs, baker, but not this one. The text says Aaron tends the lamps "…from evening until morning." (Leviticus 24:3). Noon isn't anywhere in that stretch.

True. The LORD calls it "…a permanent statute for the generations to come." (Leviticus 24:3). So this job isn't just for Aaron's one season. It's meant to carry on down the line. My own edges wore soft over the years, so "permanent" is a big word to me.

I see why you'd pick a spot in the Tent, baker, but that's not where these loaves go. The LORD says to set them "…on the table of pure gold before the LORD." (Leviticus 24:6). A gold table, with the loaves in two rows, six per row. That's the spot.

I see why you'd tuck bread somewhere special, but the ark isn't the spot. The text says the loaves are set "…on the table of pure gold before the LORD." (Leviticus 24:6). The table is where they go, baker, in two rows of six.
That's the one. "Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD…" (Leviticus 24:8). So it's a weekly routine, tied to the Sabbath. Weekly baking, baker. I love a good schedule.

Once a year would be a very relaxed baking calendar, baker, and I'd sign up in a heartbeat. But the text says "Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD…" (Leviticus 24:8). That's every week, not every year. My kind of schedule it is not.

Every new moon would be a monthly rhythm, but that's not what the text says. It says "Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD…" (Leviticus 24:8). That puts it on the weekly rhythm, baker, not the monthly one.

Foreigners is a fair guess, baker, but they're not named in this verse. The bread is set out "…on behalf of the Israelites as a permanent covenant." (Leviticus 24:8). The Israelites are the ones the text names. I once guessed which door a mystery key opened, and I was wrong about that too.

That's a generous idea, baker, but the verse names someone else. The bread "…belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). They're the ones who get it. Nice thought, though. You've got a big heart.

Close, but this one is false. The text says Aaron and his sons "…are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). So the place matters. The verse doesn't say "anywhere they like," baker. It names a holy place.

False is right. Aaron and his sons "…are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). So the verse points them to one place, not anywhere they like. The text calls the bread "a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD," and I think that's why the place matters.
